content:
alex_cheng: Heads up — after last night's kernel reorder (int8-first fallback) we're seeing 2x p99 on streaming chat for short-turn chats (~<16 tokens). p95 up ~20%. Root cause looks like microbatching policy switched batches for streaming to the bulk kernel path when MB>=4.

priya_nadar: ack. do you have numbers? is it only streaming or completions too?

alex_cheng: only streaming. quick numbers from perfbot: streaming p99 420ms -> 820ms, p95 150ms -> 180ms. completions p99 stable. KV cache hit rate for streaming requests fell ~0.6% (warmup mismatch).

marc_roberts: hmm. could be the kernel chooser: streaming path should prefer tiny-mb kernels to keep tail low. we recently relaxed the mb threshold in kernel_selector from <=2 to <=4 to boost throughput.

alex_cheng: yes — patch showed `kernel_selector.max_streaming_mb = 4`. reverting to 2 fixes tail in local test. but throughput drops ~8%.

priya_nadar: tradeoff: SLO is 200ms p99 for tier-1 customers. we can't accept 820ms. proposal: make streaming mb cap adaptive by short-turn ratio and kv_warmup flag. e.g.

```yaml
mb_strategy:
  streaming:
    max_mb_by_short_turn_ratio:
      '<0.2': 1
      '0.2-0.6': 2
      '>0.6': 3
    prefer_streaming_kernel: true
  completions:
    max_mb: 12
```

perf-bot: perf snapshot @2305120000: streaming/p99=820ms, streaming/kv_hit=94.1%, completions/p99=1200ms, completions/kv_hit=98.7% :eyes:

marc_roberts: sounds good. also add a warmup fastpath: if kv_cache_hit_rate < 96% and connection_recent_tokens < 32 -> force max_mb=1 for next 30s.

alex_cheng: will prototype knob and run canary on 10% of streaming traffic. I'll log measurements: p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, kernel_switch_count.

priya_nadar: great. tag me when canary starts. if p99 < 250ms we ship. :thumbsup:

alex_cheng: @perf-bot start canary 10% streaming with config ref: `refs/mb-tunable/streaming-warmup-v1`
